'''''Hypericum canariense''''' is a species of [[flowering plant]] in the family [[Hypericaceae]]  known by the common name '''Canary Islands St. John's wort'''. It is the sole member of '''''Hypericum''''' '''sect. ''Webbia'''''.

==Etymology==
Among its numerous aliases in Spanish are {{lang|es|granadillo}}, {{lang|es|espanta demonios}}, {{lang|es|flor de cruz}}, and {{lang|es|leña de brujas}}.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.atlasruraldegrancanaria.com/fichas_int.php?n=302 |title=Granadillo (''Hypericum canariense'') |website=Atlas rural de Gran Canaria |language=Spanish |access-date=2017-04-29}}</ref> In Finnish, the species is known as {{lang|fi|Kanariankuisma}}''.''<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://eol.org/pages/584903/overview|title=Canary Island St. Johnswort - Hypericum canariense - Overview - Encyclopedia of Life|website=Encyclopedia of Life|language=en|access-date=2018-10-23}}</ref> Its [[Binomial nomenclature|specific epithet]] ''canariense'' is a reference to the populousness of ''H. canariense'' in the [[Canary Islands]]. As such, its common names include Canary Islands St. John's wort or Canary Islands ''Hypericum''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://gd.eppo.int/taxon/HYPCN|title=Hypericum canariense (HYPCN)[Overview]{{!}} EPPO Global Database|website=gd.eppo.int|language=en|access-date=2018-10-23}}</ref>

==Distribution==
It is [[endemic]] to the [[Canary Islands]] and [[Madeira]], where it grows in low-moisture scrub and forested slopes of the five westernmost islands from {{Convert|150 to 800|m|abbr=on}}.<ref name=Bramwell>{{cite book|last1=Bramwell|first1=D.|last2=Bramwell|first2=Z.|year=2001|title=Wild flowers of the Canary Islands|publisher=Editorial Rueda|location=Madrid, Spain|ISBN=84-7207-129-4}}</ref>{{rp|219}} It is also known as an [[introduced species]] in Australia, New Zealand, and the US states of [[California]] and [[Hawaii]], where it is an escaped [[ornamental plant]] and generally considered a minor [[noxious weed]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://wssa.net/wssa/weed/composite-list-of-weeds/|title=Composite List of Weeds {{!}} Weed Science Society of America|website=wssa.net|language=en-US|access-date=2018-10-23}}</ref>

==Habitat==
''Hypericum canariense'' grows in clayey or sandy soils, as well as in loam. It is found along creeklines and roadsides.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://florabase.dpaw.wa.gov.au/browse/profile/20043|title=FloraBase—the Western Australian Flora|last=Attractions|first=Western Australian Herbarium, Biodiversity and Conservation Science, Department of Biodiversity, Conservation and|website=florabase.dpaw.wa.gov.au|language=en|access-date=2018-10-23}}</ref> It is also prominent in dry scrub habitats and in [[Mesic habitat|mesic forests]], often alongside ''[[Globularia salicina]]''.<ref name="iucn status 13 November 2021" />

==Description==
The species is a flowering shrub growing {{convert|2|-|3|m}} in height. Its many stems bear waxy lance-shaped leaves {{convert|5|-|7|cm}} long. The plentiful flowers each have five bright to deep yellow petals each just over a centimeter long and many yellowish whiskery [[stamen]]s. It reproduces via the seed in its [[Dehiscence (botany)|dehiscent]] dry fruits and also [[Vegetative reproduction|vegetatively]] via [[rhizome]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://vicflora.rbg.vic.gov.au/flora/taxon/bae99208-de5e-44e2-bf8d-fc05c11f2372|title=Flora of Victoria|website=vicflora.rbg.vic.gov.au|language=en|access-date=2018-10-24}}</ref>

The species is commonly misidentified as ''[[Hypericum canadense|H. canadense]]'' or ''[[Cleomella arborea]]'' because of their similar flower structure and large stamens.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.inaturalist.org/taxa/77482-Hypericum-canariense|title=Canary Island St. John's Wort (Hypericum canariense)|website=iNaturalist.org|language=en|access-date=2018-10-23}}</ref>

==Varieties==
The species has three accepted varieties:<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.gbif.org/species/3189481|title=Hypericum canariense L.|website=www.gbif.org|language=en|access-date=2018-10-23}}</ref>

* ''H. canariense'' var. ''canariense''
* ''H. canariense'' var. ''floribundum'' <small>(Dryand. ex Ait.) Bornm.</small>
* ''H. canariense'' var. ''platysepalum'' <small>(Webb & Berth.) Ceb. & Ort.</small>
